---
title: "Your Presentation Title"
author: "Your Name"
institute: "Humane & Sustainable Food Lab, Stanford University"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  beamer_presentation:
    slide_level: 2
    keep_tex: false
    pandoc_args: ["--lua-filter=suppress_title.lua"]
    includes:
      in_header: preamble.tex
    highlight: tango
classoption: "aspectratio=169"
params:
  show_title_slide: FALSE
urlcolor: blue
linkcolor: blue
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Copy required files from package to working directory
pkg_resources <- system.file("rmarkdown/templates/foodlab_presentation", 
                             package = "foodlabslides")

# Copy theme file
theme_file <- file.path(pkg_resources, "resources/beamerthemeFoodLab.sty")
if (file.exists(theme_file)) {
  file.copy(theme_file, "beamerthemeFoodLab.sty", overwrite = TRUE)
}

# Write preamble.tex
writeLines(c(
  "% Food Lab Presentation Preamble",
  "",
  "% Load the theme",
  "\\usetheme{FoodLab}",
  "",
  "% Logo",
  "\\logo{\\includegraphics[height=1cm]{foodlab-logo.png}}"
), "preamble.tex")

# Write lua filter: removes title from pandoc metadata when show_title_slide=false,
# which prevents pandoc from generating \frame{\titlepage} entirely
writeLines(c(
  "function Meta(m)",
  "  if m.params and m.params.show_title_slide ~= nil then",
  "    local val = pandoc.utils.stringify(m.params.show_title_slide)",
  "    if val == 'false' then",
  "      m.title = nil",
  "    end",
  "  end",
  "  return m",
  "end"
), "suppress_title.lua")

# Copy logo file
logo_file <- file.path(pkg_resources, "skeleton/foodlab-logo.png")
if (file.exists(logo_file)) {
  file.copy(logo_file, "foodlab-logo.png", overwrite = TRUE)
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

## Precedents from other modeling competitions for interpretability rules and cheating prevention?

- [The DREAM challenges in bio](https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn4224222/docker/) require Docker containers that organizers run.

- [Kaggle rules](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/make-it-better/rules) leave a lot of discretion to contest organizers: "Submission may be made as a model, notebook, prediction file, or other format as determined by the Sponsor."

- [Grand challenges are strict on data](https://hecktor.grand-challenge.org/Participation/): "Using additional (public or not) data for training or unsupervised training on the test data is not eligible for prizes since we want to compare models trained on the same data with a held-out test set. However, if participants want to evaluate such approaches, we can provide evaluations on the test set upon request, and they are welcome to report their work as a paper in the official proceedings."

## The Makridakis Competitions on time series methods

- [M5 uncertainty competition](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0169207021001722) had policies but also exceptions: "objectivity and reproducibility was a prerequisite for collecting any prize...the winning teams, **with the exception of companies providing forecasting services and those claiming proprietary software,** had to upload their code...no later than 14 days after the end of the competition." 
  - "Companies providing forecasting services and those claiming proprietary software had to provide the organizers with a detailed description of how their forecasts were made and a **source or execution file for reproducing them.**"
- In the [accuracy competition](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0169207021001874), "only 17 of the developers of the 50 top-performing methods shared information about their forecasting approaches, even after the organizers sent several emails requesting this information." 

## CASP is more 'anything goes'

- [Alphafold2 won CASP14 (protein folding contest) in Nov. 2020](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-021-03819-2), at which point observers [asked for source code](https://www.skeptic.org.uk/2020/12/if-googles-alphafold2-really-has-solved-the-protein-folding-problem-they-need-to-show-their-working/). 

- The DeepMind team shared the source code in 2022.

- The contest is more concerned with standardized _outputs_ than inputs.

## A real wildcard approach: incentivize prediction markets to surface all available information and let models take advantage of that

- A friend in ML research says: "start polymarket entries for the outcomes of these studies and say you'll give extra money to whoever produces the best trading bot for those markets. That way, any known/insider information is hopefully already in the baseline that these AIs are trying to beat."

- But this totally cuts against intelligibility. Is our goal a model that works or that we understand? And what are our baseline prediction models to which we're comparing entries? I think those are the big questions.
